comparator.name: Natural and Social Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–2027 Bèta-gamma regulations and published Earth Sciences major plan distinguish 75 EC of common Bèta-gamma study, 69 EC of compulsory Earth Sciences study and 36 EC of genuine electives. Recommended electives are not required major content. The Future Planet Studies regulations B-4.13 explicitly apply its entry conditions to Bèta-gamma Earth Sciences students, except for Modelling for Sustainability, and require an Earth-science thesis topic. The partial record now includes the 18 EC bachelor project and totals 174 EC. Project 4 remains excluded because the current regulations retain a discontinued Academic Skills prerequisite. The current published major plan identifies students starting the major in September 2026; students follow the plan applicable when they start their major.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is generic Bèta-gamma. Its formal OER and current catalogue list Earth Sciences first among the disciplinary majors without identifying a single broad default. Retain this neutral route selection; do not switch route to avoid the unresolved common Project 4 rule.

exception.reason: Confirm how September 2026 Bèta-gamma entrants meet the discontinued standalone Academic Skills prerequisite for Project 4. The adopted 2026–2027 Bèta-gamma OER B-4.5.5 still requires 5022AVBG3Y, while B-9.2 discontinues it with no replacement and only a resit arrangement for earlier students. An applicable replacement, amendment or authorised cohort rule is needed; examination-board discretion is not an automatic waiver.
exception.curriculumContext: The 180 EC structure is 75 EC of Bèta-gamma study, 69 EC of Earth Sciences study and 36 EC of elective space. This partial record accounts for 174 EC, including the 18 EC Earth-science bachelor project. The remaining 6 EC Project 4 has an unresolved Academic Skills admission condition for the reviewed intake.

audience.programmeDescription: Natural and Social Sciences (Bèta-gamma) combines natural and social sciences at the University of Amsterdam. Students study a common first year, then specialise in a major while continuing interdisciplinary project work.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Bèta-gamma combines a shared natural- and social-science foundation with a disciplinary major and interdisciplinary projects. With Earth Sciences, the published plan includes 36 EC of genuine elective space. The table accounts for 174 EC; a complete UCR comparison awaits clarification of the remaining Project 4 entry condition for the 2026 intake.

curriculum.limitation: The degree is 180 EC. This partial table shows 174 EC and leaves out the 6 EC Project 4 while its Academic Skills entry condition remains unresolved. Major courses and elective space follow the published plan; students use the plan applicable when they start their major.

componentNotes.uva-open-electives: The Earth Sciences plan leaves 36 EC for genuine electives. At most 12 EC may be at any bachelor level; the remaining space uses second- or third-year courses. A completed official Dutch minor can replace these level conditions. Courses must avoid excessive overlap; other arrangements require written examination-board approval.
